subject: Realtime inference latency spike - reserved pool impact
messages:
From: Kate Allen <kate.allen@nimbusretail.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@nimbusretail.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:31 -0700
Subject: Realtime inference latency spike - reserved pool impact

Alex / Marissa —

We just hit a ~3x latency spike in our checkout recommender traffic at 09:05 PDT and started seeing request timeouts from our side. This is on our reserved GPU pool (customer id NR-2025). The spike coincides with a banner campaign rollout but the traffic increase should have been within the pool's headroom. The spike caused ~2% of live checkouts to fail while we rolled back the campaign.

Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood-side routing or autoscale issue? We need a short mitigation plan and ETA — we have executives asking. Attaching a short metrics dump.

Thanks,
Kate Allen
Head of Engineering, Nimbus Retail

Attachments: nimbus-metrics-snapshot-0819.pdf (CPU/GPU metrics, p95/p99 latency)
From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Kate Allen <kate.allen@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:24:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime inference latency spike - reserved pool impact

Kate — thanks for the heads up and for the metrics snapshot. We're investigating now. Quick summary of what I'm doing immediately: 

- Pulling allocator logs and autoscaler traces for your reserved pool (NR-2025) between 08:45–09:30 PDT.
- Checking for noisy-tenant signals and kernel-level preemptions.
- Preparing a temporary routing rule: route critical checkout traffic to our hosted fallback model for up to 30 minutes (will need your signoff).

Preliminary note from an initial glance at the metrics: we see a rapid increase in queued requests at the same time as GPU kernel stalls on one node and a surge of large-batch requests from a different tenant in the same pool. That combination can exacerbate dispatch delays and cause the autoscaler to under-react.

Can you confirm if any non-standard large-batch jobs (e.g., offline eval or heavy embedding jobs) were started from your side or by partners around 09:00? If not, we'll proceed with the fallback routing and an isolation action on the noisy tenant.

I'll update in 20–30 minutes with a mitigation ETA.

— Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-incident-timeline-0819.csv (internal timeline, allocator snapshots)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:02:49 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime inference latency spike - reserved pool impact

Alex — quick internal update for the thread: I flagged the noisy tenant (tenant id t-998) and asked the pool allocator to deprioritize their burst while we confirm. Lauren, marking this as an SLA-impacting event — can you loop in legal/finance for a potential credit?

Engineers are also validating whether a recent scheduler tweak we rolled on Monday reduced headroom for mixed-batch workloads; if that's implicated we'll roll back the tweak and re-run the autoscaler simulation.

Also: Kate, if you approve, I'll initiate the hosted fallback routing now (we'll do a 30-minute block that preserves checkout traffic to avoid losses). If you prefer, we can instead temporarily add extra reserved nodes (slower to provision).

— Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Kate Allen <kate.allen@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ops@nimbusretail.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:47:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime inference latency spike - reserved pool impact

Kate / Nimbus team —

Thank you for the patience. Here's the concise incident update and immediate remediation steps we executed for NR-2025: 

Timeline (summary):
- 08:57 PDT — sudden increase in batched inference requests observed from tenant t-998 in the same reserved pool.
- 09:05 PDT — kernel-level stalls detected on node gpu-7 driven by a large contiguous KV cache flush; queued requests spiked and the autoscaler threshold did not trigger fast enough given the mixed-batch profile.
- 09:15 PDT — Redwood initiated deprioritization of tenant t-998 and enabled hosted fallback routing for your critical checkout route (approved by you at 09:18). That reduced p99 latency to near baseline within ~6 minutes.
- 09:55 PDT — monitoring confirms restored throughput; final validation completed at 10:00 PDT.

Root cause (short): the incident was caused by simultaneous noisy-tenant large-batch traffic plus an interaction with a recent scheduler tweak that reduced effective headroom for mixed small/large batch workloads. The autoscaler logic did not react quickly enough to the queue growth due to optimistic batching assumptions.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Tenant deprioritization and temporary isolation of t-998.
- Hosted fallback routing activated for the checkout route for 30 minutes (no data was routed outside of the customer tenancy beyond what the fallback requires; we respect your data controls).
- Rolled back Monday's scheduler tweak in the affected region and re-ran autoscaler sims against your traffic pattern.

Next steps and commitments:
- We will produce a full postmortem (root cause analysis, timeline, corrective actions, regression tests) by 2026-08-26.
- We propose the following technical actions: tighten noisy-tenant detection thresholds, add a fast-path autoscaler trigger for sudden queue growth, and introduce a per-pool protective headroom guard for mixed-batch workloads.
- Financial/credits: Lauren (cc'd) will follow up on an SLA credit for the impacted windows; we'll include a credit estimate with the postmortem.

Attachments included: nimbus-metrics-snapshot-0819.pdf, redwood-incident-timeline-0819.csv
Related ticket: https://redwood.app/ops/tickets/SUP-4321

If you'd like a short 15-minute call to walk the timeline and mitigation live, I'm available this afternoon.

— Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
